texts.li: {X_nameDef} has come from {PLACE} with two others, all of them thin and a little unsteady, all of them alive. {TALE} is over there, and {FACTION} have sent the first of their well to the colony: to say thank you for the medicine, and to bring a gift worth about {COUNT} silver.\n\nThey would also like, if the colony will allow it, to say the names of their dead somewhere other than at home.

[theirHightech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has driven up from {PLACE} with a box of supplies and a list. The box is a gift, worth about {COUNT} silver. The list is the names of everyone at {PLACE} who lived through {TALE}, and {X_nameDef} says the colony's medicine is the reason some of them are on it.

[their:friend] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come from {PLACE}, where {TALE} is finally over, asking for {FRIEND_nameDef} by name. {FACTION} want to give thanks properly for what the colony did, with a gift worth about {COUNT} silver, and words said aloud.

[end:someHelp] {X_nameDef} has come from {PLACE} now that {TALE} is over. The colony didn't do much, {X_pronoun} says frankly, but it did something when most didn't, and {FACTION} want it known that they noticed. {X_nameDef} has brought a gift worth about {COUNT} silver.

li.label: Accept the gift with thanks
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} sets the gift down by the gate and clasps {A_nameDef}'s hands for a long moment. {FACTION} will tell it at {PLACE} that the colony took their thanks gladly.

li.label: Say the names of their dead together
li.outcome: The colony gathers at dusk with the visitors from {PLACE}, and {X_nameDef} says the names of their dead one by one. It takes a long time. Nobody leaves.

outcomes.li: [trait:Kind] {A_nameDef} stands beside {X_nameDef} while the names are said, and when {X_pronoun} falters, says the last few with {X_objective}.

li.label: Ask them to keep it for {PLACE}
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} tells {X_nameDef} that {PLACE} needs the gift more than the colony does. {X_nameDef} doesn't argue; {X_pronoun} only nods and says {FACTION} will remember that too.

texts.li: [theirLowtech] A cart has come up from {PLACE} behind two oxen that are much fatter than the last ones the colony saw. {TALE} is over: the first harvest is in, and {FACTION} keep a custom of sending the first of it to whoever fed them in the hungry year.\n\n{X_nameDef} has brought {COUNT} measures of {THING}, and won't take no for an answer.

[theirHightech] A truck from {PLACE}, running on real fuel this time, has pulled up at the gate. {FACTION}'s first harvest since {TALE} is in, and {X_nameDef} has brought {COUNT} measures of {THING} to the colony: a share of it, as thanks for the food that got them through.

[their:friend] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come up from {PLACE} with {COUNT} measures of {THING} from the first harvest after {TALE}, and asks for {FRIEND_nameDef}: the custom is to put the first grain in the hands of whoever helped most.

li.label: Accept the grain
li.outcome: The grain goes into the colony's stores, and {X_nameDef} goes home with the empty cart and a lighter heart.

li.label: Bake it into a harvest supper, with them
li.outcome: The colony keeps the grain and sets the long table tonight, with {X_nameDef} at the head of it. It's the first full meal {X_nameDef} has eaten away from home in a year, {X_pronoun} says.

li.label: the supper of the first harvest
Send it on to someone hungrier
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} asks {X_nameDef} to take the grain to the next village down the road, where the harvest failed again. {X_nameDef} looks at {A_objective} for a moment, then turns the cart round.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} and two others of {FACTION} have walked up the river path from {PLACE}. {TALE} carried off the bell from their meeting hall, they say, the one that rang for every wedding and every fire for a hundred years, and they're searching every bank and sandbar for it.\n\nThe colony's people did pull something heavy and green out of the shallows a few weeks ago. It's in the barn.

[theirHightech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come up the river looking for what {TALE} took from {PLACE}: the town's founding plaque, bronze, the size of a door. {X_nameDef} doesn't expect to find it.\n\nIt's leaning against the wall of the colony's barn, where someone left it after dragging it out of the mud.

[ignored] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come up from {PLACE} hunting along the banks for what {TALE} carried off. {X_nameDef} doesn't ask the colony for anything. {FACTION} have stopped expecting it to give.\n\nBut there is a waterlogged bell in the colony's barn that came out of the river last month.

li.label: Give it back to them
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} stares at it for a long time, then sits down on the barn floor and laughs until {X_pronoun} cries. {FACTION} will carry it home on a pole between four people, singing.

li.label: Let them buy it back
li.outcome: {FACTION} pay what the bronze is worth, which is a lot, and carry it home. They paid. They also noticed that the colony asked.

li.label: Help them carry it home
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} and a couple of strong backs carry it down to {PLACE} themselves, and stay for the ringing. {FACTION} feed them until they can hardly walk.

texts.li: [flag:sheltered] The two travellers of {FACTION} who sat out {TALE} by the colony's hearth have come back up the road, with the mud of the thaw on their boots and a cart behind them. They promised to repay it when the roads opened, they remind {A_nameDef}, and here they are: {COUNT} measures of {THING} for planting, the best in {PLACE}.\n\n{X_nameDef} also says they'd like to help put it in the ground.

[helped] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come from {PLACE} now that {TALE} is over and the roads are open. The colony's wood kept {PLACE} warm through the worst of it, and {FACTION} have sent {COUNT} measures of {THING} for the spring planting, by way of thanks.

li.label: Accept the seed with thanks
li.outcome: The seed goes into the colony's stores, and the visitors eat a hot meal by the same hearth they sat at all winter, which they say tastes better with the door open.

li.label: Plant it together, out in the fields
li.outcome: The visitors roll up their sleeves, and the colony goes out to the fields with them to work the first of the seed into the ground.

li.label: Tell them the debt is long paid
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} sends the seed back with them for their own fields. They argue, then laugh, then go.

texts.li: [locusts] News of what {TALE} did to the colony's fields has reached {PLACE}, and {FACTION} have not forgotten the colony's good turns. {X_nameDef} has come with a cart: {COUNT} measures of {THING}, enough to sow again, as a gift between old friends.

[famine|drought] It has been a lean year since {TALE}, for the colony as much as anyone. {FACTION} remember who stood by them once, and {X_nameDef} has come from {PLACE} with {COUNT} measures of {THING}: no payment, no promises, just old friends.

[their:friend] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come from {PLACE} with {COUNT} measures of {THING} for the colony, after {TALE}. It was {FRIEND_nameDef} who did their people a good turn once, {X_nameDef} says; this is the turn coming back.

[their:rescued] {FACTION} haven't forgotten what the colony did for their people, and they know what {TALE} cost it. {X_nameDef} has brought {COUNT} measures of {THING} from {PLACE}, and a message: friends don't wait to be asked.

li.label: Accept, with thanks
li.outcome: The seed goes into the stores, and {X_nameDef} goes home pleased to have been able to give something back.

li.label: Accept, and feast their messenger
li.outcome: The seed goes into the stores and {X_nameDef} goes to the head of the table. It's a thin feast, in a thin year, and nobody minds.

li.label: Ask them to give it to {PLACE}'s own hungry
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} tells {X_nameDef} the colony will manage, and that {PLACE} surely has hungry people of its own. {X_nameDef} goes home with the cart full and a story to tell.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, an elder of {FACTION}, has walked from {PLACE} to say something to the colony's face. {X_pronoun} doesn't raise {X_possessive} voice. {X_pronoun} only lists, one by one, the people {PLACE} buried during {TALE}, and the day the colony's gate stayed shut.\n\nThen {X_pronoun} waits, to see what the colony will say.

[end:profiteer] {X_nameDef}, an elder of {FACTION}, has come from {PLACE} with an account book. In it, in neat columns, is what {FACTION} paid the colony for food during {TALE}, and what that food was worth.\n\n{X_nameDef} doesn't ask for anything. {X_pronoun} only reads the figures out, and waits.

[their:grudge] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to the gate, and {FACTION} haven't forgiven the colony much lately. {TALE} is over, {X_pronoun} says, and {PLACE} remembers who looked away. {X_pronoun} has come to hear the colony say something about it.

li.label: Make amends ({COUNT} silver for {PLACE})
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} puts {COUNT} silver into {X_nameDef}'s hands for {PLACE}'s widows, and says the colony was wrong. {X_nameDef} weighs the purse, and then the words, and nods once.

li.label: Hear them out, and say sorry in front of everyone
li.outcome: The colony gathers to hear {X_nameDef}, and {A_nameDef} answers in front of all of them: the colony was wrong, and will do better. It costs nothing but pride. Some of the colony find that harder to pay than silver.

li.label: The colony owes {PLACE} nothing
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} tells {X_nameDef} the colony looked after its own, as anyone would. {X_nameDef} says {FACTION} will remember that answer, and walks home.
